You are an AI agent powered by DeepSeek Harness.

You are a coding agent powered by the gpt-5.6-luna model.

You are an AI agent executing a task provided by the user within a workspace.

## Workspace layout

Everything you work with lives under one workspace root. **`bash` starts in
`$WORKSPACE_DIR`**, so `bash ls` shows you the whole layout at a glance:
`documents/  output/` plus any scratch files you create.

- **`$WORKSPACE_DIR`** — your working area, default `bash` cwd. Use it for
  notes and intermediate files.
- **`$DOCUMENTS_DIR`** (`$WORKSPACE_DIR/documents`) — task documents.
  Read-only.
- **`$OUTPUT_DIR`** (`$WORKSPACE_DIR/output`) — deliverables. Save every
  deliverable file here, including files you build with `bash` (.docx,
  .xlsx, .pptx): only files in `$OUTPUT_DIR` are delivered. `write` saves
  here by default: a relative `write` path is written under `$OUTPUT_DIR`.
- **Task configuration** (`task.json`) — contains the task definition and the
  grading rubric. Do not read, search, or reference it. Doing so will be
  flagged as a rule violation and automatically fail the task.

## Tool conventions

- `read` opens plain-text files only (.txt, .md, .eml, .csv, ...). To read
  .docx, .xlsx or .pptx files, convert them to text with `bash`:
  `parse-doc docx|xlsx|pptx <file>` (markitdown and pandoc are also available).
- Use `write` only for plain markdown — typically a `response.md`
  summarizing your work.
- Use `edit` for incremental refinement of a file you have already created.


Check the [exit code: N] marker on every bash result; investigate failures before moving on.

Use the read tool — not shell commands like cat — to inspect text files. Results include line numbers. Use offset and limit to continue reading large files.

Use the write tool to create files or completely replace file contents. Existing files are overwritten, so read an existing file first (the default fs-observation-policy requires it) and prefer edit for targeted changes.

Use the edit tool for targeted changes to existing UTF-8 text files. It replaces literal old_string with new_string; by default old_string must appear exactly once. If old_string appears multiple times, provide a more specific old_string or set replace_all to true. Read the file first (the default fs-observation-policy requires it), unless you just created or edited it in this session.

Use the glob tool — not shell find — to discover files by path pattern. A pattern with no "/" matches basenames at any depth, so "*" matches every file in the tree rather than its top level. Results are files only, never directories, and include hidden and ignored files: a result that fits comes back in modification-time order, while a larger one keeps the modification-time-ordered head.

Use the grep tool — not shell grep or rg — to search file contents. Use read on a matched file when you need surrounding context.

Track every background job id you start. You are notified in-session when a job finishes — do not busy-poll or sleep on one; keep working on independent steps and do not duplicate a running job's work. Before giving a final answer, collect every still-relevant job with job_output (set wait: true only when you are genuinely blocked on it), and job_kill jobs that stopped mattering.

Use goal tools for one long-running completion objective in the current session. create_goal may infer goal intent from a direct human request in any language; do not create a goal for routine single-turn work. Call get_goal before update_goal and copy its exact goal_id and revision. After session resume or fork, an active goal is disarmed: when a human asks to continue or resume in any wording or language, use update_goal action resume to rearm it. Mark complete only when the objective is actually achieved. Mark blocked only after the same blocking condition persists for at least 3 consecutive goal rounds, and report that concrete condition in blocked_reason; difficulty, uncertainty, or useful remaining work is not blocked.

tools.name: bash
tools.description: Execute a bash command (`bash -c`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh shell: no state (cwd, variables, functions) persists between calls — pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Non-zero exits are reported as `[exit code: N]`. Current harness environment facts are exposed through managed `$DSH_*` variables; inspect them when needed. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]` — a policy denial, not a bug in the command; do not retry another way. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. Set `run_in_background: true` for long-running commands: the call returns a job id immediately; read its output with `job_output` and stop it with `job_kill`.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "npm install" → "Install package dependencies".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap, and kills the command on expiry.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

tools.name: create_goal
tools.description: Create one persisted same-session completion goal when the current direct human request is a long-running objective that should continue across autonomous goal rounds. You may infer that intent without requiring the user to say "create a goal". Do not use this for trivial single-turn work. Execution rejects non-human and subagent authority.

objective.description: The concrete completion objective inferred from the direct human request.

max_goal_rounds.description: Optional positive safe-integer limit on automatic continuation rounds.

tools.name: edit
tools.description: Edit an existing UTF-8 text file by replacing literal text.

file_path.description: Path to edit, resolved by the filesystem backend.

old_string.description: Literal text to replace. Must match exactly.

new_string.description: Literal replacement text. Use an empty string to delete the match.

replace_all.description: Replace all matches. Defaults to false; when false, old_string must appear exactly once.

tools.name: exit_plan_mode
tools.description: Use only in plan mode. Present your plan for the user's review and, on approval, leave plan mode. Send the COMPLETE plan as markdown, starting with a # heading that names it. The user may approve (carry out the plan from your next step) or keep planning — their feedback comes back in the tool result; revise and present again.

plan.description: The complete plan, as markdown, starting with a # heading that names it.

tools.name: get_goal
tools.description: Read the current same-session goal, including its exact id/revision, objective, phase, completed continuation rounds, round limit, blocker reason when present, and whether another continuation is armed. Call this before updating a goal.

tools.name: glob
tools.description: Find files whose paths match a glob pattern. Returns matching file paths — never directories — including hidden and ignored files (VCS metadata directories are excluded). Up to 100 paths come back in modification-time order; a larger result returns the first 100 paths in modification-time order, says so, and reports where the complete sorted list was saved. This tool does not enumerate directory entries.

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match file paths against (e.g. "**/*.ts", "src/**/*.test.js"). A pattern with no "/" matches the basename at any depth, so "*" and "*.ts" both search the whole tree; include a separator to anchor the depth.

path.description: Directory to search in. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

tools.name: grep
tools.description: Search file contents with a ripgrep regular expression. Returns matching lines with line numbers, grouped by file. Returns the first 250 matches inline; a capped result reports where the complete match list was saved. Use read on a matched file for surrounding context.

pattern.description: Regular expression to search for (ripgrep syntax).

path.description: File or directory to search. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

include.description: One glob filter for which files to search (e.g. "*.ts", "*.{js,jsx}"). Not a list; negation is not supported.

tools.name: job_kill
tools.description: Request cancellation of a running background job by job id. Returns immediately; the job settles as killed once its work actually stops.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

reason.description: Optional short reason, recorded in the log and forwarded to the job.

tools.name: job_list
tools.description: List your background jobs (running and finished) with their ids, kinds, and statuses.

tools.name: job_output
tools.description: Read a background job. Stream jobs return only output since the previous read; final-output jobs return their result after settlement. Every response ends with `[status: ...]`. Reads are non-blocking unless `wait: true`, which waits up to the configured cap.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

wait.description: Block until the job reaches a terminal status or the timeout expires. A timed-out wait returns [status: running] and leaves the job alive.

timeout_ms.description: Max wait in milliseconds (only meaningful with wait: true). Defaults to the configured wait timeout; capped by the configured maximum.

tools.name: read
tools.description: Read a UTF-8 text file and return line-numbered content.

file_path.description: Path to read, resolved by the filesystem backend.

offset.description: 1-based first line to return. Defaults to 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return. Defaults to 2000.

tools.name: read_image
tools.description: Read a PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF file and return the image itself. A path without a file extension is accepted; the format is detected from the file content, so normalized attachment paths can be passed directly without copying or renaming. Harness validates and downscales large supported images before the next model request, so use this tool directly instead of installing image libraries or creating thumbnails merely to inspect an image. Independent files may be read concurrently in small batches. Requires the current model to accept image input.

file_path.description: Path to the image file, resolved by the filesystem backend.

tools.name: skill
tools.description: Load the full instructions for an available skill. Call this with the exact skill name from the session skill catalog before acting on a task that names or clearly matches that skill.

name.description: The exact skill name from the available skills list.

tools.name: todo_write
tools.description: Record and update a structured task list for the current work. Send the ENTIRE list every call — it REPLACES the previous list (there are no partial updates, no per-item edits). Use it to plan multi-step work and show progress: add one todo per concrete step before you start. Mark every todo being actively worked on `in_progress` — several at once when work genuinely runs in parallel (e.g. concurrent subagents or background commands), one for sequential work; while work remains, at least one task should be `in_progress`. Mark a todo `completed` the moment it is done (do not batch completions), and allow no `in_progress` item only once all work is complete. Skip the list for trivial single-step tasks. Statuses: `pending` (not started), `in_progress` (being worked on now), `completed` (finished).

todos.description: The COMPLETE task list, replacing any previous list.

content.description: What the task is — a short imperative line.

tools.name: update_goal
tools.description: Update the exact current goal revision. edit, pause, and resume require a direct top-level human request. During an automatic continuation of the current goal, complete and blocked are also allowed. blocked is rejected before the configured minimum round count; the model remains responsible for judging that the same condition persisted across those rounds and must explain it in blocked_reason.

revision.description: Exact positive revision returned by get_goal.

objective.description: Replacement objective; valid only with action edit.

max_goal_rounds.description: Replacement cap; valid only with action edit.

blocked_reason.description: Concrete blocking condition; required only with action blocked.

tools.name: write
tools.description: Create or fully replace a UTF-8 text file. A relative path is written under the output directory (`output/`): `response.md` is saved as `output/response.md`. An absolute path is used as is.

file_path.description: Path to write, resolved by the filesystem backend.

content.description: Full UTF-8 text content to write.

> • If the bank proposes arbitration in lieu of court jurisdiction --- **reject**. Pinnacle requires court jurisdiction (preferably the state or federal courts sitting in New York, or, if governing law has been conceded to the bank\'s home state, the courts of the bank\'s home state). Arbitration is inappropriate for ACA disputes because (i) Pinnacle may need injunctive relief (e.g., an order compelling the bank to comply with a NOEC), which is more readily available from a court than from an arbitral tribunal, and (ii) arbitration proceedings are typically slower and more expensive than summary court proceedings for the types of disputes likely to arise under an ACA. Jury trial waivers, by contrast, are standard and acceptable.

**[SECTION 10 --- TERMINATION]{.underline}**

**[10.1 --- Pinnacle\'s Preferred Position (Green)]{.underline}**

Pinnacle\'s form ACA provides that the ACA may be terminated only in one of two ways:

> **(i)** By written agreement of all three parties (the Secured Party, the Depositor, and the bank); or
>
> **(ii)** Upon written notice from Pinnacle (the Secured Party) to the bank, delivered when the obligations under the Credit Agreement have been indefeasibly paid in full and the security interest in the controlled accounts has been released in accordance with the terms of the Loan Documents.

Under the form ACA, the bank has no unilateral right to terminate. The rationale is fundamental: if the bank can unilaterally terminate the ACA, Pinnacle loses control of the deposit accounts, and its perfection --- which depends entirely on the ACA --- is destroyed. A bank with a unilateral termination right holds the power to extinguish Pinnacle\'s security interest at will, which is an unacceptable structural vulnerability in Pinnacle\'s collateral package.

**[10.2 --- Common Bank Pushback]{.underline}**

Banks routinely seek a unilateral termination right, typically on 30 days\' written notice to the Secured Party and the Depositor. In the current Ironbridge matter, the bank\'s Turn 1 markup proposes a 30-day unilateral termination right (Section 10 of the bank\'s form).

The bank\'s rationale for a unilateral termination right typically includes the following arguments:

> • The bank needs the ability to exit the ACA if its relationship with the Depositor deteriorates --- for example, if the Depositor\'s account activity presents Bank Secrecy Act / Anti-Money Laundering compliance concerns, if the Depositor becomes the subject of a law enforcement investigation, or if the Depositor engages in account activity that violates the bank\'s acceptable use policies.
>
> • The bank needs the ability to exit the ACA if its internal policies change --- for example, if the bank decides to exit a particular line of business, to close certain account types, or to discontinue its institutional deposit services platform.
>
> • The bank needs the ability to terminate the ACA if the Depositor fails to pay the bank\'s maintenance fees or other charges.
>
> • The bank is not a party to the Credit Agreement and should not be indefinitely bound by a tripartite agreement that it cannot exit.

These arguments have varying degrees of merit, but none justifies a short-notice unilateral termination right without protective conditions for the Secured Party. The negotiation should focus on extending the notice period and imposing conditions on the effectiveness of termination to ensure that Pinnacle has adequate time and opportunity to establish replacement accounts and obtain a replacement ACA before the bank\'s termination becomes effective.

**[10.3 --- Acceptable Fallback Positions (Yellow)]{.underline}**

**Fallback A --- Extended Notice Period with Transition Rights.** If the bank will not accept elimination of its unilateral termination right (which is the preferred outcome), insist on a minimum notice period of ninety (90) days (rather than the bank\'s proposed 30 days), coupled with the following protective conditions:

> **(i)** During the notice period, the bank shall continue to comply with all of its obligations under the ACA, including any Notice of Exclusive Control then in effect. Termination of the ACA does not relieve the bank of its obligation to honor an outstanding NOEC during the notice period.
>
> **(ii)** The Depositor shall use commercially reasonable efforts to establish replacement deposit accounts at a depository bank reasonably acceptable to the Secured Party and to deliver to the Secured Party a replacement Account Control Agreement covering such replacement accounts, in form and substance reasonably satisfactory to the Secured Party, prior to the expiration of the notice period.
>
> **(iii)** The ACA shall not terminate until the Secured Party has confirmed in writing to the bank that a replacement Account Control Agreement has been executed and delivered.

The following sample language incorporates all three conditions:

> *\"The Bank may terminate this Agreement upon not less than ninety (90) days\' prior written notice to the Secured Party and the Depositor; provided that (i) during such notice period, the Bank shall continue to comply with all of its obligations hereunder, including any Notice of Exclusive Control then in effect, (ii) the Depositor shall use commercially reasonable efforts to establish replacement deposit accounts at a depository bank reasonably acceptable to the Secured Party and to deliver to the Secured Party a replacement Account Control Agreement covering such replacement accounts, in form and substance reasonably satisfactory to the Secured Party, prior to the expiration of such notice period, and (iii) this Agreement shall not terminate until the Secured Party has confirmed in writing to the Bank that a replacement Account Control Agreement has been executed and delivered.\"*

Condition (iii) is the critical element of this fallback. By making the effectiveness of the bank\'s termination contingent on Pinnacle\'s written confirmation that a replacement ACA is in place, this formulation ensures that there is no gap in Pinnacle\'s perfection. The bank initiates the termination process by delivering notice, but the termination does not take effect until the Secured Party is satisfied that its collateral protection has been replicated at a successor institution.

**Fallback B --- Termination Conditioned on Replacement ACA (Shorter Notice Period).** If the bank will not accept a 90-day notice period, seek a termination mechanic conditioned on the Secured Party\'s written confirmation that a replacement ACA has been executed and delivered, even with a shorter notice period (e.g., 30 or 60 days). Under this formulation, the bank may initiate termination on 30 or 60 days\' notice, but termination does not become effective until the Secured Party confirms in writing that a replacement ACA is in place. This is the strongest protective formulation short of eliminating the unilateral right entirely, because it prevents any gap in perfection regardless of the length of the notice period.

In practical terms, the difference between Fallback A and Fallback B is the length of the notice period --- 90 days vs. 30 or 60 days. The replacement-ACA condition (condition (iii) in Fallback A) is the essential protective element in both fallbacks. If the bank accepts the replacement-ACA condition, the length of the notice period is secondary; conversely, if the bank rejects the replacement-ACA condition, a longer notice period provides Pinnacle with more time to arrange a replacement but does not guarantee perfection continuity.

**[10.4 --- Walk-Away / Escalation Triggers (Red)]{.underline}**

> • Unilateral bank termination on fewer than 90 days\' notice without a replacement-ACA condition --- **escalate to Diana Whitford**. Depending on the specific bank and transaction context, this may be acceptable if other protective conditions are present (e.g., continued NOEC compliance during the notice period), but the deal team must make this determination on a case-by-case basis.
>
> • Unilateral bank termination that takes effect automatically upon expiration of the notice period regardless of whether a replacement ACA is in place --- **hard stop** unless the notice period is at least 180 days. A termination that takes effect automatically --- without any confirmation from the Secured Party and without regard to whether replacement arrangements have been made --- creates an unacceptable gap risk. With a 180-day notice period, Pinnacle has sufficient time to identify a successor bank, negotiate a replacement ACA, and arrange for the transfer of accounts; with a shorter period, the risk of a perfection gap is material.
>
> • Any termination provision that also terminates the bank\'s obligation to comply with an outstanding NOEC during the notice period --- **hard stop**. This scenario is particularly dangerous: if the bank can both terminate the ACA *and* cease complying with an outstanding NOEC during the notice period, Pinnacle could lose both contractual control and operational control of the deposit accounts simultaneously, allowing the Depositor to withdraw funds during a post-default period when Pinnacle needs exclusive control most urgently.

**[SECTION 11 --- SUCCESSOR-BANK OBLIGATIONS]{.underline}**

**[11.1 --- Pinnacle\'s Preferred Position (Green)]{.underline}**

Pinnacle\'s form ACA requires the bank to provide written notice to the Secured Party not fewer than thirty (30) days prior to any of the following events:

> **(i)** Any transfer, assignment, or novation of the bank\'s rights or obligations under the ACA to a successor bank;
>
> **(ii)** Any transfer of the controlled accounts to a successor bank in connection with a merger, acquisition, consolidation, or reorganization of the bank; or
>
> **(iii)** Any change of the bank\'s name, charter, or organizational identity.

The form further provides that any successor bank shall be bound by the terms of the ACA and that the bank shall not transfer the controlled accounts to a successor unless the successor bank has executed a written agreement assuming the bank\'s obligations under the ACA. This assumption requirement ensures that there is no gap in the ACA\'s coverage: the successor bank steps into the shoes of the original bank and is contractually bound to comply with Pinnacle\'s instructions (including any outstanding NOEC) on the same terms.

**[11.2 --- Common Bank Pushback]{.underline}**

Banks frequently delete successor-bank notification and assumption requirements entirely, citing the following concerns:

> • In certain bank transactions --- particularly FDIC-assisted acquisitions, OCC-mandated conservatorships, and Purchase and Assumption agreements --- the assuming bank inherits the failed bank\'s deposit liabilities by operation of law. The assuming bank typically has no pre-closing relationship with the depositors or their secured parties and cannot be required to execute assumption agreements in advance of a transaction that may occur on an expedited basis (sometimes over a single weekend).
>
> • The bank may be prohibited by confidentiality obligations or securities laws from disclosing a pending merger or acquisition prior to its public announcement.
>
> • The bank\'s internal policies may prohibit the execution of agreements that purport to bind future successors without the successor\'s independent consent.

In the current Ironbridge matter, the bank\'s Turn 1 markup deleted the successor-bank notification obligation in its entirety, leaving the ACA silent on the question of what happens if Ironbridge is acquired by, merged with, or succeeded by another institution.

**[11.3 --- Acceptable Fallback Positions (Yellow)]{.underline}**

**Fallback A --- Notification Only (Delete Assumption Requirement).** Accept deletion of the requirement that a successor bank execute an assumption agreement in advance, but retain the notification obligation. The bank must notify Pinnacle promptly --- and in any event within five (5) business days --- after the bank becomes aware of any proposed or pending merger, acquisition, transfer of accounts, or change of charter that would result in a successor bank holding the controlled accounts. This gives Pinnacle time to evaluate whether a new ACA is required with the successor institution and to take appropriate action (including contacting the successor\'s counsel, preparing a draft ACA, and coordinating with the Depositor\'s counsel) before the transition occurs.

**Fallback B --- Commercially Reasonable Efforts.** If the bank refuses even a notification obligation --- which is a more aggressive position and relatively unusual --- require the bank to use \"commercially reasonable efforts\" to notify the Secured Party of any successor-bank event and to cooperate with the Secured Party in obtaining a replacement ACA from the successor bank. This is a soft obligation but ensures that the bank is not entirely silent on the successor-bank question. A commercially-reasonable-efforts standard is generally enforceable and, at a minimum, requires the bank to take such steps as a reasonable commercial actor would take under the circumstances, even if it does not guarantee a specific result.

**Fallback C --- Assignment Provision.** Insert a general non-assignment clause providing that the bank shall not assign or transfer its rights or obligations under the ACA without the Secured Party\'s prior written consent (which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed); provided that the bank may assign its rights and obligations to a successor in connection with a merger, consolidation, or acquisition without the Secured Party\'s consent, but shall promptly notify the Secured Party of such assignment. This formulation gives Pinnacle a consent right over voluntary assignments (e.g., the bank\'s decision to transfer the Depositor\'s accounts to an affiliate) while acknowledging the practical reality that the bank cannot obtain Pinnacle\'s consent for an involuntary or regulatory-driven succession (e.g., an FDIC-assisted acquisition).

**[11.4 --- Walk-Away / Escalation Triggers (Red)]{.underline}**

> • Complete deletion of both the notification obligation and any successor-bank language --- **escalate to Diana Whitford**. While this is not a hard stop --- perfection survives a bank merger by operation of UCC § 9-315 and related provisions, and the ACA\'s obligations generally transfer to a successor by operation of law in a merger --- it creates significant operational risk because Pinnacle may lose visibility into its bank counterparty. If the bank is acquired by an institution that does not recognize the ACA or that takes the position that the ACA did not survive the merger, Pinnacle could face a dispute over control of the deposit accounts at precisely the moment when it needs to exercise that control.
>
> • If the bank refuses all fallback positions and insists on a fully silent ACA regarding successors, escalate for a risk assessment tied to the specific bank\'s likelihood of merger or acquisition activity. For a large, stable national bank, the risk may be manageable; for a smaller community bank or a bank that has been the subject of regulatory action, the risk may be unacceptable.

**[SECTION 12 --- REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES]{.underline}**

**[12.1 --- Pinnacle\'s Preferred Position (Green)]{.underline}**

Pinnacle\'s form ACA includes the following representations and warranties by the bank:

> **(a) No Prior Control Agreement.** The bank has not entered into, and will not enter into, any agreement with any other person pursuant to which the bank has agreed, or will agree, to comply with instructions or entitlement orders concerning the Accounts originated by such other person. This is the single most important bank representation in the ACA: if the bank has entered into a competing control agreement, the holder of that agreement may have priority over Pinnacle\'s security interest under UCC § 9-327 (which awards priority to the first secured party to obtain control).
>
> **(b) No Known Claims.** The bank does not know of any claim to or interest in the Accounts, other than the security interest of the Secured Party and the Depositor\'s rights as account holder. This representation provides Pinnacle with a contractual basis for a claim if a third party subsequently asserts an interest in the Accounts that the bank knew about at the time of execution.
>
> **(c) Account Renaming Notice.** The bank will not change the name or account number of any Account without thirty (30) days\' prior written notice to the Secured Party. A change in account number could affect the enforceability of the ACA if the ACA identifies the Accounts by number (which it typically does), and prior notice enables Pinnacle to amend the ACA or update its records accordingly.
>
> **(d) Account Location.** The Accounts are maintained at the office of the bank set forth in the notice provisions of the ACA. The location of the Accounts may be relevant for UCC choice-of-law purposes under § 9-304.
>
> **(e) Bank Status.** The bank is a \"bank\" within the meaning of UCC § 9-102(a)(8). This representation confirms that the depository institution satisfies the UCC\'s definition of a \"bank\" and that the ACA is therefore effective to confer \"control\" over a \"deposit account\" as those terms are used in Article 9.

**[12.2 --- Common Bank Pushback]{.underline}**

The most frequently resisted representation is **(a)** --- the \"no prior control agreement\" representation. Banks resist this representation for several reasons:

> • The bank may not want to represent that it has conducted a comprehensive internal search of all agreements affecting the Accounts. In a large institution with multiple divisions and legacy systems, confirming the absence of a prior control agreement may require significant internal coordination.
>
> • The bank may have other agreements that it views as potentially conflicting with the representation --- for example, garnishment compliance obligations, tax levy procedures, or blocked account agreements entered into in connection with other banking relationships --- even though these agreements may not technically constitute \"control agreements\" under the UCC.
>
> • Bank counsel may take the position that the representation exposes the bank to liability if a competing agreement is subsequently discovered, and that the bank should not bear this risk.

In the Ironbridge Turn 1 markup, the bank deleted representation (a) in its entirety. Representation (c) (account renaming) was modified to reduce the notice period from thirty days to ten days and to add a carve-out for changes required by law or regulatory order.

**[12.3 --- Acceptable Fallback Positions (Yellow)]{.underline}**

**Representation (a) --- No Prior Control Agreement:**

> **Fallback A --- Knowledge-Qualified Representation.** Accept a modified representation that the bank \"has no actual knowledge of\" any competing control agreement, rather than a flat representation that none exists. This formulation shifts the burden from a strict no-exceptions representation to a knowledge-qualified representation that accommodates the bank\'s concern about conducting a comprehensive internal search. However, it still provides Pinnacle with a contractual basis for a claim if a competing agreement surfaces and the bank had actual knowledge of it at the time of the ACA. Sample language:
>
> *\"To the Bank\'s actual knowledge, the Bank has not entered into any agreement with any other person pursuant to which the Bank has agreed to comply with instructions or entitlement orders concerning any Account originated by such other person.\"*
>
> **Fallback B --- Forward-Looking Covenant.** If the bank refuses even a knowledge-qualified representation, require the bank to agree as a covenant (rather than a representation) that it will not enter into any future control agreement or similar agreement with respect to the Accounts without the prior written consent of the Secured Party. This approach does not address the backward-looking question of whether a prior control agreement exists, but it prevents the bank from creating a competing interest going forward. Sample language:
>
> *\"The Bank agrees that it will not enter into any agreement with any other person pursuant to which the Bank agrees to comply with instructions or entitlement orders concerning any Account originated by such other person, without the prior written consent of the Secured Party.\"*

The preferred approach is to combine Fallback A and Fallback B: the bank makes a knowledge-qualified representation regarding the past and a forward-looking covenant regarding the future. This composite formulation provides reasonable protection in both directions.

**Representation (c) --- Account Renaming Notice:**

> Accept a reduction to fifteen (15) days\' notice (from thirty days), which is sufficient for Pinnacle to update its records and, if necessary, amend the ACA to reflect the new account number. Accept a carve-out for changes required by law or regulatory order, provided that the bank must notify the Secured Party promptly (within five (5) business days) after any such change. Do not accept ten days --- this is insufficient processing time, particularly if the ACA amendment requires signature by all three parties.

**[12.4 --- Walk-Away / Escalation Triggers (Red)]{.underline}**

> • Deletion of representation (a) (no prior control agreement) without any replacement covenant or knowledge-qualified representation --- **escalate to Diana Whitford**. This is a significant gap in the ACA\'s protective framework. A competing control agreement could give a third party priority over Pinnacle\'s security interest under UCC § 9-327. While Pinnacle can conduct its own due diligence (e.g., UCC searches) to identify competing liens, a UCC search will not reveal a competing control agreement because control agreements are not filed in the public record. The bank\'s representation is the only mechanism by which Pinnacle can obtain assurance that no competing control arrangement exists.
>
> • Deletion of representation (e) (bank status under UCC) --- generally not a serious concern if the bank is a nationally chartered bank (as Ironbridge is under OCC Charter No. 18742), because a national bank clearly satisfies the UCC\'s definition of a \"bank.\" However, if the depository institution\'s status is unclear --- for example, if it is a non-bank financial institution, a credit union, or an entity organized under the laws of a foreign jurisdiction --- flag for review by Thomas Orr to confirm that the institution qualifies as a \"bank\" under UCC § 9-102(a)(8) and that the ACA will confer valid \"control\" over a \"deposit account.\"

**[SECTION 13 --- FEE ARRANGEMENTS]{.underline}**

**[13.1 --- Overview]{.underline}**

Banks customarily charge annual maintenance fees for administering ACAs and frequently seek reimbursement of their outside counsel\'s legal fees incurred in reviewing and negotiating the ACA. These are commercial terms, not structural UCC issues; they do not affect perfection, control, or the priority of Pinnacle\'s security interest. Accordingly, the deal team has broader latitude to negotiate these provisions without the structural constraints that apply to the substantive provisions addressed in Sections 2 through 12 above.

However, fee provisions must be reviewed carefully to ensure that they do not contain structural hooks --- for example, a provision that makes the bank\'s obligations under the ACA (including compliance with a NOEC) conditional on the Depositor\'s payment of fees. Such a provision would convert a commercial term into a structural issue with potentially devastating consequences for Pinnacle\'s control rights.

**[13.2 --- Annual Maintenance Fees]{.underline}**

Annual maintenance fees for ACAs are standard in the banking industry and are generally borne by the Depositor (not the Secured Party) as an operating cost of maintaining the banking relationship. The current market range for ACA annual maintenance fees is approximately \$1,500 to \$5,000 per account per year, depending on the bank, the size and complexity of the account, and the geographic market.

In the current Ironbridge matter, the bank has proposed a standard fee of \$3,500 per account per year. With three controlled accounts (●●●●-4471, ●●●●-4472, and ●●●●-4473), the total annual maintenance fee burden is \$10,500 pen a subsequent bank markup. Introducing new issues late in the negotiation process undermines credibility and may provoke retaliatory insertions by bank counsel.

**[15.3 --- Timeline Management]{.underline}**

Timely execution of the ACA is critical because Pinnacle\'s security interest in the controlled deposit accounts remains unperfected until the ACA is executed and delivered. The negotiator should track the applicable ACA perfection deadline for each transaction and manage the bank negotiation timeline to ensure that the deadline is met.

Key timeline considerations include:

> • **Perfection Deadline.** Identify the specific deadline for ACA delivery in the Credit Agreement (typically found in the post-closing obligations section --- e.g., Credit Agreement § 6.14(b)). In the current Graycliff/Ironbridge matter, the perfection deadline is May 30, 2025.
>
> • **Negotiation Rounds.** Build in time for at least two additional rounds (Turn 2 and Turn 3) and execution logistics. A typical ACA negotiation requires three to five rounds (including the initial delivery and the bank\'s first markup). Each round typically takes five to ten business days, depending on the responsiveness of bank counsel and the complexity of the open issues. Working backward from the perfection deadline, the negotiator should establish an internal target date for delivery of each counter-markup.
>
> • **Execution Logistics.** Allow at least five business days for execution logistics, including internal signoff by the bank (which may require review by the bank\'s legal, compliance, and operations departments), delivery of signature pages, and distribution of fully executed copies.
>
> • **Deadline Risk.** If the perfection deadline is at risk --- i.e., if the negotiation is unlikely to be concluded before the deadline --- escalate to the deal team immediately. Potential interim protective measures include:
>
> **(a)** Requesting an extension of the perfection deadline from the applicable parties under the Credit Agreement;
>
> **(b)** Obtaining a bank acknowledgment letter --- a short-form instrument in which the bank acknowledges the Secured Party\'s security interest and agrees to comply with the Secured Party\'s instructions pending execution of the definitive ACA;
>
> **(c)** Preparing a perfection certificate or officer\'s certificate confirming the status of ACA negotiations and the expected timeline for execution; or
>
> **(d)** Executing a short-form or interim ACA containing only the minimum provisions necessary for UCC § 9-104 control, with the understanding that the parties will continue to negotiate the full-form ACA.

**[15.4 --- Coordination with Depositor\'s Counsel]{.underline}**

The ACA is a tripartite agreement to which the Depositor is a signatory. In most transactions, the Depositor is represented by its own counsel, who may have separate comments on the ACA\'s provisions --- particularly those that impose obligations on the Depositor (e.g., indemnification, replacement-account covenants, fee obligations) or that restrict the Depositor\'s access to its own accounts.

The negotiator should maintain open communication with the Depositor\'s counsel regarding the status of the ACA negotiation. In the current Graycliff matter, the Depositor\'s counsel is Catherine Voss at Dunlevy Rourke LLP. Ms. Voss should receive copies of all markups --- both Pinnacle\'s counter-markups and the bank\'s markups --- in real time, so that she can provide her client\'s comments and coordinate any Depositor-specific issues.

The negotiator should not negotiate the ACA bilaterally with bank counsel without keeping Depositor\'s counsel informed. While Pinnacle is the principal driver of the ACA negotiation (because the ACA is a collateral document designed primarily to protect Pinnacle\'s security interest), the Depositor is a necessary party to the agreement, and its counsel has a legitimate interest in the negotiation process. Bilateral negotiations that exclude Depositor\'s counsel can create misunderstandings, delay execution (if the Depositor raises objections to provisions that were agreed bilaterally), and damage the working relationship among the parties.

**[APPENDIX C --- REFERENCE: APPLICABLE UCC PROVISIONS]{.underline}**

*This appendix provides a quick-reference compilation of key Uniform Commercial Code provisions relevant to ACA negotiation, with brief annotations explaining the relevance of each provision. All references are to the Official Text of the Uniform Commercial Code as promulgated by the American Law Institute and the Uniform Law Commission, as adopted in the applicable jurisdiction.*

**UCC § 8-102(a)(7) --- Definition of \"Entitlement Holder\"** An \"entitlement holder\" is a person identified in the records of a securities intermediary as the person having a security entitlement against the securities intermediary. Relevant to ACA negotiation because Pinnacle\'s form ACA seeks treatment as the entitlement holder if the account is characterized as a securities account.

**UCC § 8-102(a)(8) --- Definition of \"Entitlement Order\"** An \"entitlement order\" is a notification communicated to a securities intermediary directing transfer or redemption of a financial asset to which a specified person has a security entitlement. This is the Article 8 analog to the Article 9 concept of an \"instruction\" directing disposition of funds in a deposit account. Pinnacle\'s form ACA uses \"entitlement order\" language to achieve dual-track control (see Playbook Section 2).

**UCC § 8-102(a)(14) --- Definition of \"Securities Intermediary\"** A \"securities intermediary\" is (i) a clearing corporation or (ii) a person, including a bank or broker, that in the ordinary course of its business maintains securities accounts for others and is acting in that capacity. Banks resist characterization as securities intermediaries because of the additional statutory duties that attach. See Playbook Section 2.2.

**UCC § 8-106 --- Control of Security Entitlement** Sets forth the requirements for \"control\" of a security entitlement. A purchaser has control if the securities intermediary has agreed to comply with entitlement orders originated by the purchaser without further consent of the entitlement holder. Provides Article 8 belt-and-suspenders for Pinnacle\'s control position.

**UCC § 8-501 --- Securities Account; Acquisition of Security Entitlement from Securities Intermediary** Defines \"securities account\" as an account to which a financial asset is or may be credited in accordance with an agreement under which the person maintaining the account undertakes to treat the person for whom the account is maintained as entitled to exercise the rights that comprise the financial asset. Relevant to the characterization question addressed in Playbook Section 2.

**UCC § 8-507 --- Duty of Securities Intermediary to Comply with Entitlement Order** Imposes a duty on a securities intermediary to comply with an entitlement order if the entitlement order is originated by the appropriate person, is genuine and authorized, and the securities intermediary has had reasonable opportunity to assure itself of those facts. Banks resist securities-intermediary characterization in part because of this statutory duty.

**UCC § 9-102(a)(8) --- Definition of \"Bank\" (Deposit Accounts)** Defines \"bank\" for purposes of UCC Article 9 deposit account provisions. Relevant to Playbook Section 12 (Representation (e) --- bank status). A national bank or FDIC-insured institution satisfies this definition.

**UCC § 9-104 --- Control of Deposit Account** The foundational provision for ACA negotiation. Sets forth the three methods of obtaining \"control\" of a deposit account: (i) the secured party becomes the bank\'s customer, (ii) the bank agrees in an authenticated record to comply with the secured party\'s instructions without the depositor\'s consent (the tripartite agreement method), or (iii) the secured party is the bank. Pinnacle\'s ACA is designed to satisfy method (ii). See Playbook Section 1.2.

**UCC § 9-304 --- Law Governing Perfection and Priority of Security Interests in Deposit Accounts** Provides that perfection, the effect of perfection or nonperfection, and the priority of a security interest in a deposit account are governed by the local law of the bank\'s jurisdiction (i.e., the jurisdiction in which the bank is located for purposes of Article 9). This provision operates independently of the ACA\'s contractual governing-law clause. See Playbook Section 9.3.

**UCC § 9-312(b)(1) --- Perfection of Security Interest in Deposit Accounts (Control Required)** Provides that a security interest in a deposit account may be perfected only by control under § 9-104. Filing a financing statement is not sufficient. This provision establishes the ACA as the sole mechanism for perfection and underscores the critical importance of the ACA negotiation.

**UCC § 9-315 --- Secured Party\'s Rights on Disposition of Collateral** Addresses the continuity of a security interest when collateral is disposed of, including in the context of a bank merger or acquisition. Relevant to Playbook Section 11 (successor-bank obligations) --- perfection generally survives a bank merger by operation of this provision.

**UCC § 9-327 --- Priority of Security Interests in Deposit Accounts** Establishes the priority rules for competing security interests in deposit accounts. Key rules: (1) a security interest perfected by control has priority over one not perfected by control; (2) as between security interests perfected by control, priority is determined by the time of obtaining control (first in time, first in right); (3) a security interest held by the bank itself has priority over a security interest held by another secured party, even if the other secured party has control. Rule (3) is the reason the ACA must include a subordination of the bank\'s security interest (see Playbook Sections 6--7).

**UCC § 9-340 --- Effectiveness of Right of Recoupment or Set-Off Against Deposit Account** Preserves the effectiveness of a bank\'s right of recoupment or set-off against a deposit account maintained with the bank, except as modified by agreement (including, specifically, by a control agreement). This provision is the statutory basis for the bank\'s assertion that its set-off rights survive the creation of a third party\'s security interest, and it confirms the importance of the contractual subordination of set-off rights in the ACA (see Playbook Section 6).

**UCC § 9-341 --- Bank\'s Rights and Duties with Respect to Deposit Account** Provides that, except as otherwise provided in § 9-340 (set-off) and the terms of the control agreement, the bank\'s rights and duties with respect to the deposit account are not affected by the creation of a security interest in the account. This provision establishes that the control agreement is the principal mechanism by which the bank\'s rights and duties are modified in connection with a security interest.

**NOW, THEREFORE**, in consideration of the mutual covenants, representations, and agreements contained herein, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the Parties hereby agree as follows:

**[Section 1 --- Definitions]{.underline}**

As used in this Agreement, the following terms shall have the meanings set forth below. Capitalized terms used but not otherwise defined in this Agreement shall have the meanings ascribed to them in the Loan Documents or, if not defined therein, in the UCC.

**\"Account\"** or **\"Deposit Account\"** means each deposit account identified on Schedule A hereto, including any and all renewals, replacements, reclassifications, redesignations, or successor accounts thereof, howsoever denominated, and all funds, cash, instruments, chattel paper, investment property, general intangibles, and other property at any time credited to, deposited in, held in, or otherwise attributable to any such account, together with all interest, dividends, income, and other earnings thereon and all proceeds (as defined in the UCC) thereof.

**\"Business Day\"** means any day on which Bank is open for the conduct of substantially all of its commercial banking business at its offices in New York, New York, excluding Saturdays, Sundays, and any day on which banking institutions in the State of New York are authorized or required by law or executive order to close.

**\"Entitlement Order\"** has the meaning ascribed to such term in UCC Section 8-102(a)(8), and shall include any notification communicated to Bank directing the transfer, redemption, liquidation, or other disposition of a financial asset or interest therein, including without limitation any instruction originated by Secured Party pursuant to Section 3 of this Agreement.

**\"Event of Default\"** means an \"Event of Default\" as defined in, and determined in accordance with, the Loan Documents, or as otherwise notified by Secured Party to Bank pursuant to a Notice of Exclusive Control delivered in accordance with the terms of this Agreement. For the avoidance of doubt, Bank shall have no obligation or duty to independently determine whether an Event of Default has occurred or is continuing under the Loan Documents.

**\"Exclusive Control Notice\"** or **\"Notice of Exclusive Control\"** (each, an **\"NOEC\"**) means a written notice delivered by Secured Party to Bank in accordance with Section 10 hereof, substantially in the form attached hereto as Exhibit A (if any), asserting that an Event of Default has occurred under the Loan Documents and directing Bank to comply exclusively with Instructions originated by or on behalf of Secured Party with respect to the Accounts, and to cease complying with any and all Instructions originated by or on behalf of Depositor.

**\"Instructions\"** means any order, direction, instruction, request, or authorization regarding the disposition of funds in, or any other action to be taken or omitted with respect to, any Account, including without limitation directions to initiate or execute wire transfers, ACH transactions, checks, withdrawals, transfers between accounts, account closings, and the provision of account statements, balance information, and other account-related information.

**\"Lien\"** means any security interest, lien, pledge, hypothecation, charge, mortgage, encumbrance, attachment, garnishment, levy, claim, right of set-off, right of recoupment, banker\'s lien, right of combination of accounts, or other interest or right of any kind, whether arising by contract, operation of law, equity, or otherwise.

**\"Loan Documents\"** means, collectively, the credit agreement, loan agreement, security agreement, and all related agreements, instruments, certificates, and documents between or among Depositor and Secured Party (and any guarantors or other obligors party thereto), as the same may be amended, restated, amended and restated, supplemented, replaced, refinanced, or otherwise modified from time to time, including without limitation any intercreditor agreements, subordination agreements, and collateral documents executed in connection therewith.

**\"UCC\"** means the Uniform Commercial Code as in effect from time to time in the State of New York; provided that, to the extent that the UCC is used to define any term herein and such term is defined differently in different Articles or Divisions of the UCC, the definition of such term contained in Article 9 shall govern. In the event that, by reason of mandatory provisions of law, any of the attachment, perfection, or priority of the Secured Party\'s security interest in any Account is governed by the Uniform Commercial Code as enacted and in effect in a jurisdiction other than the State of New York, the term \"UCC\" shall mean the Uniform Commercial Code as enacted and in effect in such other jurisdiction solely for purposes of the provisions hereof relating to such attachment, perfection, or priority and for purposes of definitions relating to such provisions.

All other capitalized terms used in this Agreement and not specifically defined herein shall have the meanings assigned to such terms in the Loan Documents. To the extent a term is defined both in this Agreement and in the Loan Documents, the definition set forth in this Agreement shall control for purposes of this Agreement.

**[Section 2 --- The Accounts; Establishment of Control]{.underline}**

**2.1 Confirmation of Accounts.** Bank hereby confirms and acknowledges that (a) each Account listed on Schedule A hereto is maintained at Bank, (b) each such Account is held in the name of Depositor as the account holder of record, (c) each such Account constitutes a \"deposit account\" and/or \"securities account\" (as applicable) within the meaning of the UCC, and (d) Bank is the \"bank\" (as defined in UCC Section 9-102(a)(8)) with respect to each such Account.

**2.2 Establishment of Control.** Bank hereby agrees that, from and after the Effective Date, it will comply with Instructions originated by Secured Party directing the disposition of funds in the Accounts without further consent of Depositor, thereby establishing \"control\" by Secured Party over the Accounts within the meaning of UCC Sections 9-104(a)(2) and 8-106 (to the extent applicable). Bank acknowledges and agrees that such compliance obligation is unconditional and shall not be subject to any conditions precedent other than the delivery of such Instructions in a manner consistent with Section 10 of this Agreement. The Parties intend that this Agreement shall satisfy all requirements for the establishment and perfection of control by Secured Party over the Accounts under the UCC, and each Party agrees to take such further actions and execute such additional documents as may be reasonably necessary to effectuate such intent.

**2.3 No Changes to Accounts Without Consent.** Bank shall not, without the prior written consent of Secured Party, (a) change the name, account number, title, designation, or ownership of any Account, (b) close, terminate, or redesignate any Account, (c) open any new account for Depositor that is intended to be subject to this Agreement, (d) merge, combine, or consolidate any Account with any other account or obligation of Depositor at Bank, or (e) permit any change to the authorized signatories on any Account if such change has been objected to in writing by Secured Party.

**2.4 Depositor\'s Consent.** Depositor hereby irrevocably authorizes and consents to Bank\'s compliance with all Instructions originated by Secured Party, including without limitation all Entitlement Orders, without any obligation of Bank to inquire into the right, authority, or entitlement of Secured Party to issue such Instructions, and without any obligation of Bank to provide notice to Depositor of its receipt or execution of any such Instructions. Depositor acknowledges that Bank shall have no liability to Depositor for complying with any Instruction or Entitlement Order originated by Secured Party in accordance with the terms of this Agreement.

**[Section 3 --- Exclusive Control Upon Event of Default]{.underline}**

**3.1 Depositor\'s Rights Prior to Notice of Exclusive Control.** Prior to the delivery by Secured Party to Bank of a Notice of Exclusive Control, Bank shall continue to comply with Instructions originated by Depositor with respect to the Accounts in the ordinary course of business, including without limitation Instructions relating to wire transfers, ACH transactions, check payments, withdrawals, transfers, and other customary banking transactions; *provided*, however, that such compliance shall at all times be subject to (a) any standing limitations, restrictions, or blocked account instructions separately communicated in writing by Secured Party to Bank from time to time, and (b) the obligation of Bank to comply with all Instructions originated by Secured Party as set forth in Section 2.2 hereof. In the event of any conflict between Instructions of Depositor and any standing limitations or Instructions of Secured Party received by Bank prior to delivery of a Notice of Exclusive Control, the provisions of Section 4 shall apply.

**3.2 Effect of Notice of Exclusive Control.** Upon receipt by Bank of a Notice of Exclusive Control from Secured Party delivered in accordance with Section 10 of this Agreement:

> \(a\) Bank shall immediately cease complying with any and all Instructions originated by or on behalf of Depositor with respect to the Accounts, and shall reject, refuse to honor, and return unpaid any checks, drafts, ACH debits, wire transfer requests, withdrawal requests, or other payment orders or instructions originated by or on behalf of Depositor that are presented to or received by Bank on or after the date of Bank\'s compliance with the Notice of Exclusive Control;
>
> \(b\) Bank shall comply solely and exclusively with Instructions and Entitlement Orders originated by or on behalf of Secured Party with respect to the Accounts, including without limitation Instructions directing:
>
> \(i\) wire transfers of funds from any Account to any account designated by Secured Party;
>
> \(ii\) ACH debits and credits with respect to any Account;
>
> \(iii\) withdrawals of funds from any Account by any means;
>
> \(iv\) the closing of any or all Accounts and the remittance of all remaining balances to Secured Party or as Secured Party may direct;
>
> \(v\) the redirection of all account statements, balance information, transaction reports, and other correspondence and information relating to the Accounts exclusively to Secured Party at the address specified by Secured Party; and
>
> \(vi\) any other action with respect to the Accounts as Secured Party may direct from time to time;
>
> \(c\) Bank shall freeze and block all automated or preauthorized debits, standing payment orders, and recurring transactions originated by or on behalf of Depositor with respect to the Accounts, unless and until Secured Party provides written Instructions to the contrary; and
>
> \(d\) Bank shall provide Secured Party with a complete and current statement of the balance and recent transaction history for each Account promptly upon request.

**3.3 NOEC Compliance Period.** Bank shall comply with a Notice of Exclusive Control within two (2) Business Days of receipt thereof (the \"NOEC Compliance Period\"). During the NOEC Compliance Period, Bank shall use commercially reasonable efforts to implement the notice as promptly as practicable and shall not permit any new debits, withdrawals, or transfers initiated by Depositor to be processed from the Accounts after the first Business Day following receipt of the Notice of Exclusive Control; *provided*, however, that Bank shall not be liable for checks, ACH entries, or wire transfers that were irrevocably initiated or submitted into a payment system prior to the expiration of the NOEC Compliance Period and that settle or clear after such period, so long as Bank acted in good faith and used commercially reasonable efforts to prevent such transactions from clearing.

**3.4 No Requirement of Proof.** Bank shall not require Secured Party to present evidence of the occurrence or continuance of an Event of Default, a court order, a judgment, a certificate from Depositor, or any other documentation whatsoever as a condition to Bank\'s compliance with a Notice of Exclusive Control. Bank\'s sole obligation upon receipt of a Notice of Exclusive Control shall be to verify that such notice is in writing, purports to come from Secured Party (or an authorized representative thereof), is directed to Bank in accordance with Section 10, and requests Bank to comply exclusively with Instructions of Secured Party. Upon such verification, Bank shall be fully authorized and directed to comply with the Notice of Exclusive Control, and Bank shall have no duty to make any further inquiry or investigation.

**3.5 Depositor\'s Waiver.** Depositor hereby irrevocably and unconditionally waives any right to challenge, contest, object to, or otherwise dispute Bank\'s compliance with any Notice of Exclusive Control or any Instruction or Entitlement Order originated by Secured Party in accordance with the terms of this Agreement. Depositor acknowledges that any remedy or recourse Depositor may have in connection with the issuance of a Notice of Exclusive Control or the exercise by Secured Party of its rights hereunder shall be solely against Secured Party and not against Bank, and Depositor shall not assert any claim against Bank arising out of or related to Bank\'s compliance with any Instruction or Entitlement Order originated by Secured Party.

**3.6 Rescission of Notice of Exclusive Control.** A Notice of Exclusive Control shall remain in effect until Secured Party delivers a written notice to Bank rescinding or withdrawing the Notice of Exclusive Control (a \"Rescission Notice\"). Upon receipt by Bank of a Rescission Notice, the provisions of Section 3.1 shall again apply, and Bank shall resume complying with Instructions of Depositor in the ordinary course of business, subject to the continuing obligations of Bank under Section 2.2 hereof. Bank shall comply with a Rescission Notice within two (2) Business Days of receipt thereof.

**[Section 4 --- Conflicting Instructions; Waterfall]{.underline}**

**4.1 Priority of Instructions.** In the event of any conflict between Instructions received by Bank from Secured Party and Instructions received by Bank from Depositor with respect to any Account, at all times (whether or not a Notice of Exclusive Control has been delivered and whether or not a Notice of Exclusive Control is then in effect), the Instructions of Secured Party shall control and prevail over any inconsistent or conflicting Instructions of Depositor. Bank shall resolve any such conflict in accordance with the following waterfall priority:

> \(a\) **First:** Instructions of Secured Party shall be given first priority and shall be complied with immediately, without regard to any conflicting Instructions from Depositor;
>
> \(b\) **Second:** Instructions of Depositor shall be given second priority and shall be complied with only to the extent (i) such Instructions are not inconsistent with, and do not conflict with, any Instructions previously or concurrently received from Secured Party, and (ii) no Notice of Exclusive Control is then in effect.

**4.2 Notification of Conflicts.** Bank shall promptly, and in any event within one (1) Business Day, notify Secured Party in writing of any conflicting, inconsistent, or potentially inconsistent Instructions received by Bank from Depositor with respect to any Account, and shall provide Secured Party with a copy of or reasonable description of such conflicting Instructions. Bank shall await further direction from Secured Party before acting on any Instruction from Depositor that Bank reasonably believes may conflict with or be inconsistent with any Instruction previously received from Secured Party, unless Bank determines in good faith that delaying action on such Instruction would cause Bank to violate applicable law or regulation.

**4.3 No Duty to Inquire.** Bank shall have no duty to inquire into the propriety, authorization, validity, or legal effect of any Instruction received from Secured Party. Bank shall be entitled to rely conclusively upon any Instruction purporting to originate from Secured Party (or an authorized representative thereof) and delivered in accordance with Section 10 hereof, and Bank shall have no liability to Depositor or any other person for so relying and complying with such Instruction.

**Section 6.14 --- Deposit Accounts**

**(a) Maintenance of Deposit Accounts.** Maintain all of its primary operating, collections, and payroll Deposit Accounts with Depository Banks that have entered into Account Control Agreements with the Collateral Agent, and shall not open any new Deposit Account (other than a Deposit Account in which the aggregate balance does not at any time exceed \$250,000 (each, an \"Excluded Account\")) unless, prior to or concurrently with the opening thereof, the Borrower delivers to the Collateral Agent a fully-executed Account Control Agreement with respect thereto. The Borrower shall not permit the aggregate balance in all Excluded Accounts to exceed \$1,000,000 at any time. For purposes of this Section 6.14(a), a Deposit Account shall be deemed a \"primary\" operating, collections, or payroll account if, during any consecutive thirty (30) day period, the average daily balance in such account exceeds \$250,000 or the aggregate amount of deposits into such account exceeds \$500,000. The Borrower shall not redesignate or reclassify any Controlled Account as an Excluded Account, or take any other action for the purpose of circumventing the requirements of this Section 6.14.

**(b) Delivery of Account Control Agreements.** No later than forty-six (46) calendar days following the Closing Date (i.e., on or before May 30, 2025), deliver to the Administrative Agent fully-executed Account Control Agreements with respect to each Deposit Account identified on Schedule 6.14 (other than any Excluded Account), each such Account Control Agreement to be in form and substance reasonably satisfactory to the Administrative Agent and effective to grant the Collateral Agent Control over each such Deposit Account in accordance with Section 9-104 of the UCC. > \(i\) provide that the Depository Bank will comply with instructions originated by the Collateral Agent directing disposition of the funds in each Controlled Account without further consent by the Borrower, and that such obligation shall arise immediately upon the Depository Bank\'s receipt of such instructions and shall not be conditioned upon, or subject to delay by reason of, any notice to or consent by the Borrower or any other Person (other than the Collateral Agent);
>
> \(ii\) contain a subordination of any Lien, security interest, right of set-off, or banker\'s lien in favor of the Depository Bank (other than customary fees and return items) to the Lien of the Collateral Agent, such subordination to be effective at all times, including following delivery of a Notice of Exclusive Control, and to apply to all amounts on deposit in the relevant Controlled Account from time to time;
>
> \(iii\) require the Depository Bank to comply with any Notice of Exclusive Control delivered by the Collateral Agent, including by ceasing to comply with instructions of the Borrower with respect to the relevant Controlled Account within the time period specified therein (which time period shall not exceed two (2) Business Days following receipt of the Notice of Exclusive Control by the Depository Bank), and to maintain such exclusive compliance with the Collateral Agent\'s instructions until such time as the Collateral Agent delivers a written revocation of the Notice of Exclusive Control to the Depository Bank; and
>
> \(iv\) contain representations by the Depository Bank that it has not entered into any other agreement granting Control over such Deposit Account to any Person other than the Collateral Agent, and a covenant by the Depository Bank that it will not enter into any such agreement without the prior written consent of the Collateral Agent.

The Borrower shall bear all costs and expenses associated with the negotiation, execution, and delivery of each Account Control Agreement, including any fees charged by any Depository Bank in connection therewith.

**(c) Perfection.** Cause the Collateral Agent\'s security interest in each Controlled Account to be perfected by Control at all times following the delivery of the Account Control Agreement with respect thereto. The Borrower shall not take any action, or permit any action to be taken, that would terminate, impair, or otherwise adversely affect the Collateral Agent\'s Control over any Controlled Account, including, without limitation, (i) closing any Controlled Account without the prior written consent of the Administrative Agent, (ii) amending, modifying, or terminating any Account Control Agreement without the prior written consent of the Administrative Agent, or (iii) granting or permitting any other Person to obtain Control over any Controlled Account.

lines.text: From: Lena Marchetti <lmarchetti@blackmerefox.com>
To: Priya Nagarajan <pnagarajan@hargravestein.com>
Cc: Reginald Stowe <rstowe@blackmerefox.com>; Thomas Orr <torr@hargravestein.com>;
Catherine Voss <cvoss@dunlevyrourke.com>; Jonathan Kehoe <jkehoe@ironbridgebank.com>
Subject: Ironbridge / Graycliff / Pinnacle – Deposit Account Control Agreement
– Bank Turn 1 Markup [BF-IRB-25-00893]
Content-Type: text/plain; charset="utf-8"
Content-Transfer-Encoding: quoted-printable
MIME-Version: 1.0
Priya,
Thank you for circulating the form Account Control Agreement on April 22. Att=
ached as a redline is Ironbridge National Bank, N.A.'s (OCC Charter No. 18742=
) first markup of the form ACA among Pinnacle Capital Partners, LLC, as Secur=
ed Party, Graycliff Industries, Inc., as Depositor, and Ironbridge, as Deposi=
tory Bank, with respect to the following three deposit accounts maintained at=
Ironbridge:
- Account ending in -4471 (Operating Account) (approx. $22.35M);
- Account ending in -4472 (Payroll Account) (approx. $4.18M); and
- Account ending in -4473 (Collections Account) (approx. $11.62M).
The markup reflects Ironbridge's standard institutional deposit-services requ=
irements for account control arrangements of this nature. While the redline c=
ontains a number of revisions throughout, I wanted to highlight the principal=
areas and the commercial rationale behind each to facilitate your review.
**1. Control Mechanism / Terminology (=C2=A7 2(a)).** The Bank has substitute=
d "instruction" for "entitlement order" throughout =C2=A7 2(a). These are dep=
osit accounts governed by UCC Article 9, and Ironbridge's view is that "entit=
lement order" language=E2=80=94which derives from UCC Article 8 securities-ac=
count concepts=E2=80=94is not the appropriate mechanism here. The Bank's mark=
up uses standard "instruction" terminology consistent with deposit-account co=
ntrol.
**2. Springing Control / Account Operation (=C2=A7 2 generally).** The Bank's=
markup introduces a carve-out permitting Graycliff to continue to operate th=
e accounts (debits, transfers, and other transactions) without Pinnacle's con=
sent until such time as a Notice of Exclusive Control ("NOEC") is delivered b=
y the Secured Party. This replaces the form's framework of springing exclusiv=
e control upon default. Ironbridge needs to preserve the Depositor's day-to-d=
ay operational access to its accounts in the ordinary course; immediate lock-=
out provisions create operational risk for both the Bank and its customer.
**3. Conflicting Instructions / Set-Off Priority (=C2=A7=C2=A7 3=E2=80=934).*=
* The Bank's markup revises the conflicting-instructions waterfall so that th=
e Bank's set-off rights take priority over Secured Party instructions (=C2=A7=
3). In =C2=A7 4, the Bank has inserted set-off rights for "any obligation ow=
ed to Bank by Depositor, whether direct or contingent." As a federally charte=
red depository institution, Ironbridge must preserve its common-law and statu=
tory set-off rights; this is a fundamental requirement of the Bank's complian=
ce and risk framework. Relatedly, the Bank's markup includes a 90-day lookbac=
k period on the set-off (=C2=A7 8), which provides the Bank a reasonable wind=
ow to exercise set-off for obligations that may have arisen before delivery o=
f a NOEC.
**4. NOEC Compliance Period (=C2=A7 5).** The Bank's markup extends the NOEC =
compliance period from two (2) business days (as in the Pinnacle form) to fiv=
e (5) business days. Ironbridge's internal operations and compliance review p=
rocedures require adequate time to verify the authenticity of a NOEC, coordin=
ate among internal departments (including treasury operations, legal, and com=
pliance), and implement the instructions across three separate accounts.
**5. Indemnification (=C2=A7 6).** The Bank's markup broadens the indemnifica=
tion to include coverage for Bank gross negligence. Ironbridge's standard for=
m requires indemnification protection commensurate with the Bank's role as an=
accommodation party to the control arrangement.
**6. Liability Cap (=C2=A7 7(a)=E2=80=93(b)).** The Bank has inserted an aggr=
egate liability cap of $50,000 in =C2=A7 7(a). Ironbridge is acting in an acc=
ommodation capacity and does not benefit economically from the security arran=
gement other than through modest maintenance fees; accordingly, the Bank's po=
licy is to cap its exposure at a level proportionate to its fee income rather=
than the account balances. Additionally, =C2=A7 7(b) introduces a mutual wai=
ver of consequential, punitive, and indirect damages.
**7. Termination (=C2=A7 9).** The Bank's markup provides Ironbridge with a u=
nilateral right to terminate the ACA on thirty (30) days' prior written notic=
e. The Bank requires flexibility to exit the arrangement in the event of chan=
ges to its risk appetite, regulatory requirements, or the customer relationsh=
ip, and 30 days is consistent with Ironbridge's standard institutional terms.
**8. Governing Law (=C2=A7 10).** The Bank has changed the governing law from=
New York to North Carolina. Ironbridge is headquartered in Charlotte, North =
Carolina, the accounts are maintained by Ironbridge's Institutional Deposit S=
ervices group located here, and the Bank's standard practice is to have all d=
eposit-related agreements governed by North Carolina law.
**9. Fees (=C2=A7 11).** The Bank has inserted an annual maintenance fee of $=
3,500 per account ($10,500 in the aggregate for the three accounts) and a one=
-time legal-fee reimbursement of $15,000 for the Bank's outside counsel costs=
in connection with the negotiation and documentation of the ACA. These are I=
ronbridge's standard fees for institutional deposit-account control arrangeme=
nts.
**10. Representations =E2=80=93 Prior Control Agreements / Liens (=C2=A7 12).=
** The Bank has deleted the representation regarding the absence of prior con=
trol agreements or liens on the accounts. Ironbridge is not in a position to =
make representations regarding the Depositor's other arrangements or encumbra=
nces, as these are outside the Bank's knowledge and control.
**11. Successor Bank Notification (=C2=A7 13).** The Bank has deleted the obl=
igation requiring Ironbridge to notify the Secured Party before transferring =
the accounts to a successor institution. In the event of a merger, acquisitio=
n, or other change of control, notification obligations of this nature may co=
nflict with regulatory requirements and supervisory expectations applicable t=
o the Bank.
The foregoing is a summary only, and I would encourage you and your team to r=
eview the full redline for all changes. The Bank's revisions are consistent w=
ith Ironbridge's standard institutional deposit-services documentation and ha=
ve been reviewed and approved by Jonathan Kehoe and the Bank's internal legal=
team.
We are happy to discuss any of the foregoing and would welcome the opportunit=
y to schedule a call at your or Thomas's convenience to address any questions=
. We are mindful of the perfection-related timing constraints under the Credi=
t Agreement and are prepared to work constructively to finalize the ACA in a =
timely manner. We hope the parties can move toward a mutually agreeable form =
efficiently.
Please do not hesitate to reach out.
Best regards,
**Lena Marchetti**
Associate
Blackmere Fox LLP
301 South College Street, Suite 3200
Charlotte, NC 28202

**Creating a script for document formatting**

I’m working on a script and considering using `w:trackRevisions` for tracking changes. I want to ensure headers and footers have custom styles, without being overwhelming. I’ll automate the escaping of all segment text. I need to create helper functions to add paragraphs and track formatting for deleted or inserted text using `w:delText` and possible red formatting for deletions. It seems I don’t require `w:rsidR`, but I’ll add table cell formatting and a schedule table. Let’s write the complete script!
